choices.content: First multiply the first equation by 2, then subtract them.

question.prompt: When solving the system \(\begin{cases}x+y=7\\x-y=3\end{cases}\), what should be done to the two equations to eliminate \(y\)?

solutions.explanation: The coefficients of \(y\) are \(1\) and \(-1\), which are opposites. Adding the two equations eliminates \(y\), giving \(2x=10\).
solutions.title: Add opposite coefficients
